claims_disputed.claim: Specifying a database engine is the most damaging single constraint; ORM's marginal effect is small (and helps GPT-5.2)
claims_disputed.reason: Requiring PostgreSQL/SQLite adds real implementation work, not just a constraint: the engine must be used and the schema 'created automatically at server startup' (§3.2). L0 leaves persistence unspecified, so the matched-pair delta (Table 3a) conflates 'constraint' with 'more functionality'. The ± stderr also averages over pairs × configurations without clustering by configuration or framework.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: The regex-based static verifiers are only an evaluation gate, never fed back to the agent. App. D shows enforcing them changes A% by at most 2.7 pp, so the paper gives no evidence that static/lint feedback in the loop helps.

missed_issues: hype_language / overclaim: §5.1 says decay is 'steep, universal', but Table 2 has non-monotonic cases: GPT-5.2 A% goes 27.1 at L2 to 48.0 at L3; GPT-5.4 pass@1 is 64.6 at L3 vs 62.5 at L0; Kimi-K2.5 pass@1 is 33.3 at L3 vs 8.3 at L2. These are subset configurations with only 4 tasks × 3 runs per level.
other:constraint_vs_workload_confound: the database constraint adds persistence work (see disputed claim), so 'constraint decay' is partly 'task-size growth'.
The LLM-judge validation labels come from 'one of the authors' (App. B), a single annotator with no inter-rater check.
The feature-implementation sanity check (Table 3b) has no L0 counterpart, so it cannot show decay, only that the tasks are hard.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats. This is the most team-relevant paper in the batch (OpenAPI contract plus structural constraints), but its headline mixes constraint load with added persistence work, and 'universal' is contradicted by several non-monotonic rows.
